newsitem.title: UK: Hardy Oil sees benefits from new reserves.
newsitem.headline: Hardy Oil sees benefits from new reserves.

text.p: Britain's Hardy Oil & Gas Plc said on Tuesday its commercial proven and probable reserves nearly doubled last year due to successful discoveries.
The company said reserves at December 31 1996 amounted to 88 million barrels of oil equivalent (mboe), compared with 54 mboe at March 31, 1996.
It also announced a net profit of 5.7 million pounds compared to a loss of 6.6 million pounds in the year to March, 1996.

John Walmsley, the group's chief executive described the year under review as an "excellent period", saying it had not only improved financially, but had added new commercial reserves and succesfully appraised some recent discoveries.
"The refocusing we began two years ago is now complete," Walmsley said.
Hardy Oil has signed a new agreement with a group of banks for a 200 million pound revolving credit facility to finance future investment and acquisition opportunities, it said.
The group pencilled the Elgin/Franklin and Banff reserves in the North Sea and Miano in Pakistan as having strong potential for the future.
Along with PY-3 in India and Bayu/Undan in Australia, these developments are seen trebling Hardy Oil's production in next six years.
The first production well Indian PY-3 offshore field has tested a flow rate of over 6,500 barrels per day of 49 API oil.
First oil from the field is expected in the second half of 1997 with production of over 10,000 barrels of oil per day expected in the begining.
Hardy is planning a total of 17 exploration and appraisal wells in India, Pakistan and in Australia.
"...Shareholders have every reason to look forward with confidence to the coming year," Walmsley said.
